n: This short psalm, headed ‘A Psalm of praise’ (or ‘thanksgiving’), invites every land on earth to shout joyfully to the Lord.

f.g: A loud shout of homage, as when greeting a king.

n: Serving God should be done with joy, not grudgingly. Coming into his presence with song is the right attitude of worship.
Know that the Lord is God and that he made us. An alternate Hebrew reading says ‘and we are his.’ Either way, we belong to him as sheep to a shepherd.

f.g: Many manuscripts read ‘and his we are’ — the two Hebrew words sound alike.

n: Worshipers are invited through the temple gates and into its courts with thanks and praise on their lips.

f.w: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving

n: Three reasons to praise: the Lord is good, his covenant love lasts forever, and his faithfulness endures through every generation.
